{{nihongo|'''Kuwayama Shrine'''|鍬山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tanba Province]].

'''Kuwayama Shrine'' (Kuwayama Shrine) is located in {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}{{ill|Kameoka, Kyoto|ar|كاميوكا|azb|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|ce|Камеока|ceb|Kameoka-shi|cs|Kameoka|de|Kameoka|eo|Kameoka|es|Kameoka (Kioto)|eu|Kameoka (Kyoto)|fa|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|fi|Kameoka|fr|Kameoka|gl|Kameoka|id|Kameoka, Kyōto|it|Kameoka|ja|亀岡市|ko|가메오카시|lt|Kameoka|mg|Kameoka|my|ခမဲအိုခမြို့၊ ကျိုတို|mzn|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|nl|Kameoka|pl|Kameoka|pt|Kameoka|ro|Kameoka|ru|Камеока|simple|Kameoka, Kyoto|sv|Kameoka|tg|Камеока|th|คาเมโอกะ|tl|Kameoka, Kyoto|tr|Kameoka|tt|Камеока|uk|Камеока|ur|کامی اوکا، کیوٹو|vi|Kameoka, Kyōto|war|Kameoka, Kyoto|zh|龜岡市|zh_classical|龜岡市|zh_min_nan|Kameoka-chhī|zh_yue|龜岡|qid=Q633996}}Kamiyada Town. In {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|Fu-sha|qid=Q134917326|lt=Fusha}}. It is also commonly known as ``Yada-sha'' or ``Yada-miya''.

=== Overview ===
It is enshrined at the eastern foot of Mt. Menkoyama in the southern part of {{ill|Kameoka, Kyoto|ar|كاميوكا|azb|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|ce|Камеока|ceb|Kameoka-shi|cs|Kameoka|de|Kameoka|eo|Kameoka|es|Kameoka (Kioto)|eu|Kameoka (Kyoto)|fa|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|fi|Kameoka|fr|Kameoka|gl|Kameoka|id|Kameoka, Kyōto|it|Kameoka|ja|亀岡市|ko|가메오카시|lt|Kameoka|mg|Kameoka|my|ခမဲအိုခမြို့၊ ကျိုတို|mzn|کامه‌اوکا، کیوتو|nl|Kameoka|pl|Kameoka|pt|Kameoka|ro|Kameoka|ru|Камеока|simple|Kameoka, Kyoto|sv|Kameoka|tg|Камеока|th|คาเมโอกะ|tl|Kameoka, Kyoto|tr|Kameoka|tt|Камеока|uk|Камеока|ur|کامی اوکا، کیوٹو|vi|Kameoka, Kyōto|war|Kameoka, Kyoto|zh|龜岡市|zh_classical|龜岡市|zh_min_nan|Kameoka-chhī|zh_yue|龜岡|qid=Q633996}}. Many ancient ruins remain in the surrounding area, including Mt.

In the {{ill|Kameoka Basin|Q11181997|qid=Q11181997}}, which is said to have been a lake in ancient times, the enshrined deity {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Oomi Takamikoto (Ōkuninushi)}} This shrine is based on the legend that, as part of the efforts to build the country, {{ill|Hozu Gorge|ja|保津峡|zh|保津峽|qid=Q10887680}} was excavated to create a basin, and the hoes used for the excavation were piled up here.

Within the fence of the precincts, Hachiman Shrine is built alongside the main shrine in the same size and style, and both shrine buildings are registered as {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture Registered Cultural Properties|ja|京都府指定・登録文化財一覧|qid=Q11375201|lt=Kyoto Prefecture Registered Cultural Properties}}. Many autumn leaves are planted in the precincts, and it is also a famous spot for autumn leaves. In addition, the annual festival ``{{ill|Kameoka Festival|ja|亀岡祭|qid=Q11370928}}'' is a traditional festival in Kameoka City, where people carry the gods to Kameoka City.

=== Enshrined God ===
* Kuwayama Shrine: '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōmi Takamikoto}}''' (Onamuchi no Mikoto)
*: Okuninushi is the same as {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} and is an Izumo god. It is said to be the main deity that has been enshrined since its founding.
* Hachiman Shrine: '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Honda Beszon}}''' (Hondawake no Mikoto)
*: Honda Besson is the same as {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}, and {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}}. It is said to be a guest deity that has been enshrined since the first year of {{ill|Eiman|Q1193868|qid=Q1193868}} ({{ill|1165|Q19676|qid=Q19676}}).
The divine crest of Kuwayama Shrine is a rabbit, in honor of Okuninushi no Mikoto, and that of Hachiman Shrine is a dove, as is customary.

=== History ===

=== Legend ===
[[File:Hozukyō (Kameoka).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Entrance to the traditional site of {{ill|Hozu Gorge|ja|保津峡|zh|保津峽|qid=Q10887680}}}}{{small|{{ill|Uketa Shrine|ja|請田神社|qid=Q11631810}} on the left bank, {{ill|Kuwada Shrine|ja|桑田神社|qid=Q11537594|lt=Kuwata Shrine}} is enshrined there. }}]]

==== Founding of Kuwasan Shrine ====
Regarding the founding of Kuwayama Shrine, there is a legend in the "Yada no Saiki" written in the first year of {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} ({{ill|1673|Q7617|qid=Q7617}}). </ref>. According to this, in ancient times, Izumo Okami and Yagami colluded with Mt. Kurogara to develop the {{ill|Kameoka Basin|Q11181997|qid=Q11181997}}, which was a mud lake. He then rides an oak boat and cuts open the Uketa Gorge (currently the mouth of {{ill|Hozu Gorge|ja|保津峡|zh|保津峽|qid=Q10887680}}), and succeeds in draining the water in the direction of {{ill|Yamashiro Province|Q749276|qid=Q749276}}, thus creating a vast plain. Izumo Okami was enshrined at the foot of Mt. Amaoka and was revered as Kuwayama Daimyojin. Additionally, this god did not attend the October (Kannazuki) meeting in Izumo Province, but the eight gods in the county met at Kuwayama Shrine <ref name=chimei/>. It is also said that the name of the shrine was given to Kuwayama because the hoes used for excavation were piled up there. </ref> (Also see "{{ill|Kameoka Basin|Q11181997|qid=Q11181997}}").

==== Hachimangu Shrine's solicitation ====
[[File:Kuwayama-jinja koike.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|A small pond between Kuwayama Shrine and Hachiman Shrine}}{{small|It is said that it was established so that the two shrines would not fight each other. }}]]
Regarding the parallel Hachiman Shrine, it is said in "Yada no Saiki" that it descended to Mt. Menfuri (Mt. Amaoka) in the first year of {{ill|Eiman|Q1193868|qid=Q1193868}} ({{ill|1165|Q19676|qid=Q19676}}). Since then, it has been enshrined as Shin Hachimangu Shrine next to Kuwayamagu Shrine, but there were thunderstorms and fights between pigeons and rabbits. The villagers thought this was a discord between the two gods, and it is said that the conflict was resolved by moving Hachimangu Shrine to Sugitani <ref name=chimei/>. Although it is unclear whether this is related to the legend, Kuwayama Shrine currently uses a rabbit, and Hachiman Shrine uses a pigeon.

Even after both shrines were moved to their current location in {{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}}14 ({{ill|1609|Q6762|qid=Q6762}}), a small pond was built between the two shrines to prevent conflicts, and the pond still exists today.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Kuwayama-jinja kuwayamagū-2.jpg|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Kuwayamamiya}}]]
[[File:Kuwayama-jinja hachimangū-2.jpg|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Hachimangu Shrine}}]]
The main shrine, Kuwayamagu Shrine, and Hachimangu Shrine are located within the same fence, with Kuwayamagu Shrine on the left and Hachimangu Shrine on the right. Kuwayama Shrine's {{ill|Munafuda|ja|棟札|zh|上樑記牌|qid=Q8008834}} exists since {{ill|Kanshō|Q1143928|qid=Q1143928}}3 ({{ill|1462|Q6546|qid=Q6546}}).

The style is Ikkensha {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} and has {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=staggered gables}}. A one-room {{ill|Karahafu|Q977293|qid=Q977293}} shrine is attached to the front, and the roof is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=persimmon thatched}}. Both shrines are registered as Kyoto Prefecture's registered cultural properties. </ref><ref>[http://spogaku.pref.kyoto.lg.jp/asset/1280.html Kuwayama Shrine Precinct Shrine Hachiman Shrine Main Hall] (Kyoto Prefecture homepage). </ref>.Based on the legend that Kuwayama Shrine and Hachiman Shrine were not on good terms, a small pond was built between the two shrines.

'''{{ill|Otabisho|Q11489117|qid=Q11489117}}'''
* Katahara Shrine (Yokomachi, Kameoka City, {{Wiki coordinates|35|00|39.21|N|135|34|51.70|E|region:JP-26|location|name=Katahara Shrine (Otabisho)}})
*: Enshrined in the ruins of a mansion south of Kameyama Castle in the center of Kameoka. Katahara Shrine is a shrine dedicated to the first lord of {{ill|Tanba-Kameyama Domain|Q10854981|qid=Q10854981|lt=Kameyama Clan}}, {{ill|Matsudaira Nobumine|Q8515964|qid=Q8515964}}, and was founded in 1898. Katahara Shrine] (Tamba Shrine [Personal Site]). </ref>. During the annual festival (Kameoka Festival), a mikoshi (portable shrine) is passed to the shrine as a traveling place.* Former Otabisho (Ichi-no-Torii) (Nakayada-cho, Kameoka City, {{Wiki coordinates|35|00|09.39|N|135|34|55.48|E|region:JP-26|location|name=Ichi-no-Torii (Old Otabisho)}})
*: This is where the Otabisho used to be, and currently there is a stone torii (Ichi-no-Torii) built by {{ill|Matsudaira Tadaharu|ja|松平忠晴|ko|마쓰다이라 다다하루 (1598년)|qid=Q11069865}} in the first year of {{ill|Jōō (Edo period)|Q1145081|qid=Q1145081}} ({{ill|1652|Q6962|qid=Q6962}}).

=== Kameoka Festival ===
The {{ill|Reisai|fr|Festival Reisai|ja|例祭|simple|Reisai|qid=Q11385469}} held in October is called ``''{{ill|Kameoka Festival|ja|亀岡祭|qid=Q11370928}}'''. In ancient times, {{ill|September 25 (Lunisolar)|Q840119|qid=Q840119|lt=September 25th}} was the Shinko Festival, and {{ill|September 30 (Lunisolar)|Q840189|qid=Q840189|lt=30th}} was the Kanko Festival<ref name=kamigami/>.

It is said that the festival at Kuwayama Shrine was abolished by {{ill|Akechi Mitsuhide|Q313320|qid=Q313320}} who invaded Tamba, but {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}}In 1681|Q7645}}, a mikoshi was donated by the lord of Kameyama Castle, {{ill|Matsudaira Tadaharu|ja|松平忠晴|ko|마쓰다이라 다다하루 (1598년)|qid=Q11069865}}<ref name=yuisho/>, and since then, the annual festival has been known as the Kameyama Festival (later Kameoka Festival), the largest festival in Kouchi-Tamba, and based on tradition, oak boats have also been paraded around the festival <ref>[http://www.k-yamahoko.com/history.html History of Yamahoko Events] ([http://www.k-yamahoko.com/index.html Kameoka Festival Homepage]) </ref>.

At the festival, 11 floats are paraded like the {{ill|Gion Matsuri|Q979873|qid=Q979873}} at {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|Q692714|qid=Q692714}} in Kyoto, and mikoshi from both Kuwayama and Hachimangu Shrines are carried to Katahara Shrine, the Otabisho.

=== Cultural assets ===

=== Kyoto prefecture registered cultural property ===
*Tangible cultural property
** Kuwayama Shrine and the Hachiman Shrine main hall (structure) - Registered on April 15, 1983 (Showa 58).
* Intangible folk cultural assets
** Kameoka Festival Yamahoko Event - The protection organization is the Kameoka Festival Yamahoko Association. Registered on March 19, 2004.

=== Kyoto Prefecture Cultural Properties Environmental Conservation District ===
* Kuwayama Shrine Cultural Property Environmental Conservation District - Decided on May 15, 1985.

=== Cultural property designated by Kameoka City ===
* Intangible folk cultural assets
** Kameoka Festival Yamahoko Event - The protection organization is the Kameoka Festival Yamahoko Association. Designated on August 3, 1998.
